title: Generic differential line of a smooth integral curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Z$ a smooth curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], where a curve is a separated integral finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension one. Let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], and put $F=k(Z)=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. Use the differential sheaf $\Omega_{Z/k}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], its stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and the module of Kähler differentials $(\Omega_{F/k},d)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. There is a unique $F$-linear isomorphism
$$\alpha_Z:(\Omega_{Z/k})_\eta\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{F/k}$$
such that for every nonempty open $W\subseteq Z$ and every $a\in\mathcal O_Z(W)$, $\alpha_Z((da)_\eta)=d(a_\eta)$, where $a_\eta\in F$ is the germ. Both vector spaces in this isomorphism have dimension one over $F$ and are nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0C1C (lemma-generically-etale), proof, invertibility of the differential sheaves and nonvanishing at the generic point; expansion by the affine localization computation in algebra.tex Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), part (2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-smooth-curve-cotangent-generic-isomorphism] with $X=Y=Z$ and $h=\mathrm{id}_Z$. Its last assertion, with $W=Z$ and $x=\eta$, says that $(\Omega_{Z/k})_\eta$ is nonzero and free of rank one over $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}=F$. Thus it has $F$-dimension one.

source.place: Tag 0C1C, lemma-generically-etale, first sentence of proof; morphisms.tex Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $\eta\in U$, $A$ is a domain, and the germ map identifies $F$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. In this affine chart $\eta$ is the prime $(0)$: its closure is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the closure of a prime $\mathfrak p$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$, so $\mathfrak p$ is contained in every prime and is zero in a domain.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, integral case; schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves

proof.text: Put $M=\Omega_{A/k}$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], $\Omega_{Z/k}|_U=\widetilde M$, compatibly with universal derivations. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] at $D(1)=U$, its section module is $M$, with $da$ corresponding to the universal differential of $a\in A$. The same statement gives quasi-coherence. Apply [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization] to this associated sheaf on $U$ at $\eta=(0)$: its germ map identifies its stalk with $(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}M$. The stalk is the ambient stalk by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: neighbourhoods contained in $U$ are cofinal, since intersecting a neighbourhood with $U$ preserves its germs.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves (2),(4),(7); morphisms.tex lemma-differentials-affine; sheaves.tex Tag 0078, stalks

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] to $k\to A$ and $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. With the preceding fraction-field identification it gives an $F$-linear isomorphism $S^{-1}M\to\Omega_{F/k}$ sending $da/s$ to $s_\eta^{-1}d(a_\eta)$. Compose with the stalk identification of step 3 to define $\alpha_Z$. In particular $\alpha_Z((da)_\eta)=d(a_\eta)$ for $a\in A$.

For any nonempty open $W$ and $a\in\mathcal O_Z(W)$, choose a basic open $D(s)\subseteq U\cap W$ containing $\eta$. Here $s\ne0$, and $a|_{D(s)}=b/s^n$ for some $b\in A$ by the basic-open section description in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Restrictions of the differential commute with $d$ by [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. The Leibniz rule of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives $d(b/s^n)=s^{-n}db-nbs^{-n-1}ds$. Applying the formula of step 4 to its germ gives exactly $d(b_\eta/s_\eta^n)=d(a_\eta)$. By the quotient presentation in the same Kähler definition, $M$ is generated by $da$ for $a\in A$; hence its localization is spanned over $F$ by their germs. The required normalization therefore determines every $F$-linear map uniquely. Finally the isomorphism transfers the dimension one and nonvanishing established in step 1 to $\Omega_{F/k}$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-fa2f1bea9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: S1 split with no new nodes and the statement unchanged; there is no re-split note, and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so no other group has superseded it. Sources read: Stacks 0C1C, whose proof starts by saying Omega_{X/k} and Omega_{Y/k} are invertible (via 02G1); 00RT(2); and 01HV. Step 1: the last clause of lem-a1-smooth-curve-cotangent-generic-isomorphism (W=Z, x=eta, h=id) gives a nonzero stalk free of rank one over O_{Z,eta}=F. Step 2: lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction gives eta in U, A a domain and F=Frac(A); eta=(0) follows elementarily from the closure V(p). Step 3: by def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, Omega|_U=(Omega_{A/k})~, which is quasi-coherent by the tilde node; lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization with L=V=U and y=eta then gives the stalk as the localization at A minus 0, and the restricted stalk equals the ambient one since neighbourhoods inside U are cofinal. Step 4: the Kahler localization node for k->A and S=A minus 0 defines alpha, with (da)_eta mapped to d(a_eta). Step 5: I checked d(b s^{-n}) = s^{-n}db - n b s^{-n-1}ds for n=0 and in characteristic p. The basic open D(s) inside U∩W exists because Z is irreducible, and uniqueness follows because the da generate the module. proof_deps equals the union of the step citations, and there is no cycle since the a1 node has no proof_deps. Small cases: A^1 (d(1/t) maps to -t^{-2}dt), an imperfect base field, and a regular but non-smooth curve, which fails the step-1 hypothesis. A grep of the DAG for Omega_{F/k}-type statements found no duplicate: the p-basis node needs k algebraically closed of characteristic p, the dominant-comparison node takes alpha as a hypothesis, and the trf/pbc nodes are ring-level. No SGA source is cited. Accepted tool_uses: lem-a1-smooth-curve-cotangent-generic-isomorphism (rank-one stalk, which no node of this unit states) and lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization (a generic sheaf fact).
